problem: The example writes 21H into STATUS and then reads TO = 0 and PD = 0 from the written bits. TO (bit 4) and PD (bit 3) of STATUS are read-only on the PIC16F877A; a write to STATUS does not change them. After power-up both are 1, so writing 21H leaves the register at 0011 0001 (TO = 1, PD = 1), not 0010 0001.
fix: Step 3 should say: IRP = 0, RP1 = 0, RP0 = 1, Z = 0, DC = 0, C = 1 are loaded from the written value; TO and PD are read-only and keep whatever they already hold (both 1 after power-up or a CLRWDT), so they are not taken from 21H. The answer for the bank (bank 1) and for C = 1 is unchanged.

problem: "STATUS 21H" and the node label "STATUS = 21H" read as if 21H were the address of the STATUS register. Section 2 correctly gives the address as 03H; 21H is only a value written into it in the worked example.
fix: Write "STATUS (address 03H) holding the value 21H, i.e. RP0 = 1" and label the node "STATUS value 21H". Keep the register address 03H separate from the value.

problem: "one 8-bit address field cannot reach all of it" clashes with Section 2, which says the direct address inside an instruction is 7 bits. A student meets 8-bit in the lead and 7-bit two paragraphs later and reads it as a contradiction.
fix: Say: the address field inside an instruction is only 7 bits, so it can name 128 locations out of the 368-byte RAM; RP1:RP0 in STATUS supply the missing high bits and split the RAM into four banks.

problem: "The 8-level stack holds return addresses for CALL only" is wrong on one point: an interrupt also pushes the return address onto the same 8-level stack when it is taken. A student may conclude interrupts do not touch the stack, which contradicts the 0004H vector explained in Section 2.
fix: Say: the 8-level hardware stack holds return addresses only, pushed by CALL and by an interrupt; it is not for data.

problem: "the ALU ... takes one operand from the working register W and the other from a file register in data memory" leaves out the literal instructions (MOVLW, ADDLW, ANDLW, IORLW, XORLW, SUBLW, RETLW), where the second operand comes from the instruction word itself, not from data memory.
fix: Add: or, for the literal instructions, from the 8-bit operand field inside the 14-bit instruction word.
